# GitPersona v0.1.1 — Security update and one-command install

Released on `2026-10-25`.

> GitPersona gives each directory its own Git identity: commits, pushes, `gh` and `glab` use the account that
> belongs to the folder you are in, in every tool that runs Git, and `gitpersona verify` proves no repository uses
> the wrong one.

## Summary

A security update. GitPersona works exactly as in v0.1.0, but it is now built with Go 1.26.10, which fixes 46
vulnerabilities in the Go standard library that the v0.1.0 binaries contained. It also brings a one-command
installer for macOS and Linux, and every download now carries signed build provenance you can check.

## Who this release is for

Everyone running v0.1.0: upgrade. Nothing in your configuration changes, and there is nothing to run afterwards.

If you have not installed GitPersona yet, this is also the easiest version to start with: one command, and the
installer picks the right build for your Mac or Linux machine.

## What you can do now

**Run a patched build.** The binaries are built with the newest Go 1.26 patch release, so Go's security fixes reach
you. Every release from now on is built the same way, and CI fails if a known vulnerability is reachable from
GitPersona's code.

**Install with one command.** `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/weikxs/gitpersona/main/install.sh | sh`
detects macOS or Linux and Apple silicon, Intel, x86_64 or arm64, checks the download against `checksums.txt`,
installs to `~/.local/bin` without `sudo`, and adds it to your `PATH`. Run it again to upgrade.

**Check where a download came from.** `gh attestation verify <file> --repo weikxs/gitpersona` proves that a file
was built by this repository's release workflow from the `v0.1.1` tag, and was not changed afterwards.

## What's new

### Security

- **Built with Go 1.26.10** instead of Go 1.26.0. The 46 fixed vulnerabilities are in the Go standard library,
  mostly in `net/http`, `crypto/tls`, `crypto/x509` and `html/template` (GO-2026-4599 to GO-2026-6809;
  `govulncheck -mode=binary` on a v0.1.0 binary lists them all). GitPersona's own code and its dependencies had
  none. The web console only listens on 127.0.0.1, which limits the exposure, but you should still upgrade.
- **Signed build provenance** for every archive and package of the release.

### Installing

- **`install.sh`** for macOS and Linux, tested on Apple silicon and Intel Macs, Linux x86_64 and arm64, and in
  Debian, Ubuntu, Alpine and Fedora. It never uses `sudo`, refuses a download whose checksum does not match, and
  changes nothing but the binary and one marked `PATH` line in your shell's startup file. `--version`, `--dir` and
  `--no-modify-path` change that.

### Release pages

- Release notes like this one, written for people deciding whether to install or upgrade, instead of a list of
  commits.

## Privacy and security

- **Never stores tokens.** GitHub tokens stay in `gh`; other hosts' tokens stay in your system keychain or Git
  Credential Manager. GitPersona keeps no copy and never prints them.
- **Never reads your keys.** Private key files are only checked to exist; ssh uses them, GitPersona never opens them.
- **Local only.** The web console listens only on 127.0.0.1, behind a link that works once, and stops after 15
  minutes without use. There is no telemetry.
- **Only when you ask.** It connects to the network only to read your accounts' public names and emails during
  setup, and to the SSH hosts when you run `check-ssh` or `verify --ssh`.
- **This release** fixes 46 Go standard-library vulnerabilities (see "What's new") and adds signed build provenance.

## Install

- Script (macOS and Linux, fully automatic): `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/weikxs/gitpersona/main/install.sh | sh`
- Homebrew (macOS and Linux): `brew install weikxs/tap/gitpersona`, or `brew upgrade gitpersona`
- Go 1.26+: `go install github.com/weikxs/gitpersona/cmd/gitpersona@v0.1.1`
- A package or archive below; check it against `checksums.txt`

| File | Platform |
|---|---|
| `gitpersona_0.1.1_darwin_arm64.tar.gz` | macOS, Apple silicon |
| `gitpersona_0.1.1_darwin_amd64.tar.gz` | macOS, Intel |
| `gitpersona_0.1.1_linux_amd64.deb` / `_arm64.deb` | Debian, Ubuntu (x86_64 / arm64) |
| `gitpersona_0.1.1_linux_amd64.rpm` / `_arm64.rpm` | Fedora, RHEL (x86_64 / arm64) |
| `gitpersona_0.1.1_linux_amd64.apk` / `_arm64.apk` | Alpine (x86_64 / arm64) |
| `gitpersona_0.1.1_linux_amd64.pkg.tar.zst` / `_arm64.pkg.tar.zst` | Arch (x86_64 / arm64) |
| `gitpersona_0.1.1_linux_amd64.tar.gz` / `_arm64.tar.gz` | Any Linux (x86_64 / arm64) |

Then sign in to each GitHub account once with `gh auth login`, and run `gitpersona setup --web`.

## Compatibility

- macOS 12 or newer on Apple silicon and Intel; Linux on x86_64 and arm64 (glibc or musl: Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora,
  Arch, Alpine and others). Windows is planned.
- Git 2.31 or newer (2.36 or newer if you have your own `includeIf "hasconfig:…"` rules).
- For GitHub profiles, the GitHub CLI 2.40 or newer; for other hosts, a credential helper such as the system keychain
  or Git Credential Manager.
- The web console is in English and Simplified Chinese; the command line is in English.

## Notes

- The macOS binary is not signed by Apple yet; Homebrew and the install script remove the quarantine flag. See
